raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Purpose

Part of [#65042](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/65042)

This is a documentation-consistency change.

`vllm serve` parses its arguments with `FlexibleArgumentParser`, which rewrites underscores in option names to dashes before the options are looked up, so both spellings are accepted:

```bash
--hf_overrides    == --hf-overrides
--tokenizer_mode  == --tokenizer-mode
--config_format   == --config-format
--load_format     == --load-format
```

The underscore spellings were therefore not broken, they were only inconsistent with the rest of the docs, which use the dash-separated spelling of the very same options:

- `docs/models/pooling_models/scoring.md` used `--hf_overrides` in five places, while the same page documents `--hf-overrides`.
- `docs/features/tool_calling.md` mixed `--tokenizer_mode`, `--config_format` and `--load_format` with the dash form `--tool-call-parser` on the same line.

This PR makes the two pages use the dash-separated spelling consistently.

Documentation-only change; no code is touched.

## Test Plan

Every `vllm serve` command in the two pages was replayed against the option parser that `vllm serve` actually builds, i.e. `FlexibleArgumentParser` with `EngineArgs.add_cli_args` (`vllm/engine/arg_utils.py`) and `FrontendArgs.add_cli_args` (`vllm/entrypoints/common/cli_args.py`).

With `FlexibleArgumentParser`, all documented commands parse with either spelling, before and after this change. The same commands fail on the underscore spelling only when the options are registered on a plain `argparse.ArgumentParser`, i.e. without the underscore-to-dash rewrite.

## Test Result

- `docs/models/pooling_models/scoring.md`: 0 underscore-style options left, 0 unresolved options in the documented `vllm serve` commands.
- `docs/features/tool_calling.md`: 0 underscore-style options left, 0 unresolved options in the documented `vllm serve` commands.

Hi maintainers, could you please add the `verified` label to this PR?

This PR only touches documentation, but the `pre-run-check` job in `.github/workflows/pre-commit.yml` currently fails with:

> To reduce unnecessary pre-commit runs, each PR must have the 'verified', 'ready', or 'ready-run-all-tests' label, or the author must have at least 4 merged PRs (found 0).

I don't have write access to label the PR myself, so I'm asking here. The `verified` label ("Run pre-commit for new contributors without triggering other tests") looks like the right fit, since this PR is docs-only and doesn't need the full test suite.

This also unblocks the Read the Docs build. `.readthedocs.yaml` runs `bash docs/pre_run_check.sh` in `post_checkout`, and that script waits for the `pre-run-check` check-run and exits 1 when it has failed, so the docs build is reported as failed even though the failure comes from the label gate rather than from the documentation itself.

- `docs/features/tool_calling.md` and `docs/models/pooling_models/scoring.md`.

Thanks!

Every documented `vllm serve` command in the two pages parses with either spelling, before and after this change; the same commands fail on the underscore spelling only with a plain `argparse.ArgumentParser`, i.e. without the underscore-to-dash rewrite.
- **Commit message**: amended to drop the incorrect "rejected with unrecognized arguments" claim and to describe the change as making the two pages consistent with the rest of the docs (same tree, no code change).

The doc change itself is kept: `docs/features/tool_calling.md` and `docs/models/pooling_models/scoring.md` now consistently use the dash-separated spelling that the rest of the docs use for the very same options.

Hi @taneem-ibrahim - thanks for the review, you are right that my replay used the raw `argparse` registrations without the `FlexibleArgumentParser` step. The PR is updated accordingly:

- **Validation**: redone with the parser that `vllm serve` actually builds (`FlexibleArgumentParser` + `EngineArgs.add_cli_args` + `FrontendArgs.add_cli_args`). Every documented `vllm serve` command in the two pages parses with either spelling, before and after this change; the same commands only fail on the underscore spelling with a plain `argparse.ArgumentParser`, i.e. without the underscore-to-dash rewrite.
- **Commit message**: amended to drop the incorrect "rejected with unrecognized arguments" claim (same tree, no code change).

Could you take another look? The doc change itself is kept: `docs/features/tool_calling.md` and `docs/models/pooling_models/scoring.md` now use the dash-separated spelling consistently with the rest of the docs.

Could a maintainer also add the `verified` label? The `pre-run-check` job fails without it ("each PR must have the 'verified', 'ready', or 'ready-run-all-tests' label, or the author must have at least 4 merged PRs"), which also blocks the Read the Docs build, even though the failure comes from the label gate and not from the documentation. This PR is docs-only.

The same label is needed for #65040 (the remaining docs pages, updated with the same feedback) and #65043 (Apple Silicon / Metal weight note) - both are docs-only as well.

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

vllm serve uses FlexibleArgumentParser, which converts underscores to dashes.  Could you update the description to describe this as documentation consistency, and use FlexibleArgumentParser for validation? Your replay probably used the raw argparse registrations without that step.
